src-wcrf-aicr-cup-2018 dis-breast dis-crc dis-endometrial severe obesity — bmi ≥40 kg/m² (who class iii obesity), distinct from the broader rf-lifestyle-obesity-cancer-prevention (which covers bmi ≥30 class i-iii). severe obesity carries multiplicative cancer-risk effects (linear-then-accelerating dose-response per wcrf/aicr + iarc working group on obesity-related cancers) particularly for hormonally- driven cancers: endometrial (rr ~7-10 vs. ~1 baseline), esophageal adenocarcinoma (rr ~4-5), post-menopausal breast cancer (rr ~1.5-2), colorectal (rr ~1.5-2), renal cell carcinoma (rr ~2), hepatocellular carcinoma (rr ~2-4 via nafld/mash), pancreatic adenocarcinoma (rr ~2). severe obesity also defines the bariatric-surgery-candidate cohort (bmi ≥40 alone, or bmi ≥35 with obesity-related comorbidity), and bariatric surgery has documented cancer-incidence reduction (~30% relative reduction for hormonally-driven cancers in long-term follow-up cohorts). categorized as chronic_condition rather than lifestyle because severe obesity carries metabolic + endocrine pathophysiology distinct from sedentary-only lifestyle elevation. prevention-persona redflag — complementary to (not redundant with) rf-lifestyle-obesity-cancer-prevention.   v0.3 wave-n niche pathway — severe obesity (bmi ≥40) prevention. fires on documented bmi ≥40 kg/m² or bmi ≥35 with documented obesity-related comorbidity (t2dm, sleep apnea, nafld, hypertension, hyperlipidemia) — the bariatric-surgery-candidate cohort definition. distinct finding name from the broader-obesity rf (which fires on bmi_ge_40 alone) so that the engine can present both tracks when applicable but they are not redundant (severe obesity opens bariatric-surgery pathway + intensified screening discussion that the general obesity rf does not specifically cover). engine routes to preventionplan recommending: (a) ind-severe-obesity-cancer-prevention-intensified (standard) — structured weight-loss intervention with multidisciplinary bariatric program (medical weight loss including glp-1 agonists / semaglutide / tirzepatide, behavioral, surgical referral when bmi ≥40 alone or bmi ≥35 entries.search_text: rf-uveal-melanoma-bap1-mut-candidate uveal (intraocular — choroidal, ciliary-body, iris) melanoma with somatic bap1 loss-of-fu... red flag red flag  src-civic src-nccn-melanoma-2025 dis-melanoma uveal (intraocular — choroidal, ciliary-body, iris) melanoma with somatic bap1 loss-of-function mutation or loss of bap1 nuclear staining by ihc. bap1-loss in uveal melanoma is the strongest single prognostic marker for metastasis-prone disease — class-2 gep (gene-expression profile) tumors per harbour 2010 / onken 2010 carry ~70-80% 5-year metastasis rate vs. ~5% for class-1 (bap1- intact) tumors. metastatic uveal melanoma was historically unresponsive to ici (orr <5% with anti-pd-1 mono; orr ~12-18% with ipi/nivo combo) due to low tmb; tebentafusp (gp100 × cd3 immtac, imcgp100-202 phase 3, nathan nejm 2021) is the first approved systemic therapy for hla-a*02:01+ metastatic uveal melanoma, with mos 21.7 vs 16.0 mo vs investigator-choice. informational at mvp: uveal melanoma is not a separately-modeled disease (dis-uveal not defined); rf surfaces (a) the bap1-loss → high-metastasis-risk prognostic shift and (b) tebentafusp hla-a*02:01 testing prompt for metastatic disease.   **why uveal melanoma is biologically distinct from cutaneous:** uveal arises from choroidal/ciliary/iris melanocytes (neural-crest origin, post-migration to the eye), drivers are gnaq / gna11 / cysltr2 / plcb4 (gαq-pathway, ~95%), not braf / nras / nf1. mutational burden is ~10× lower than cutaneous (low tmb → poor ici substrate). bap1 (3p21) is the second hit in ~50% of metastatic-prone uveal — the seminal harbour science 2010 finding that linked bap1-loss to class-2 gep and metastatic dissemination. **prognostic stratification (uveal-specific):** - class-1a gep (bap1-intact, low prame): 5-yr metastasis ~2-5% - class-1b gep (bap1-intact, high prame): 5-yr metastasis ~20% - class-2 gep (bap1-loss): 5-yr metastasis 70-80% liver is the dominant metastatic site (>90% of metastases involve liver as first site). **therapeutic implications (metastatic uveal):** - hla-a*02:01-positive: tebentafusp (fda-approved 2022) — required hla testing before treatment selection. mos 21.7 mo (imcgp100-202). cytokine-release toxicity dominates — initial inpatient or monitored-outpatient escalation per protocol. - hla-a*02:01-negative: ipilimumab + nivolumab off-label (per gem1402 / single-arm phase 2 data, orr ~18%, mos ~13 mo) — clinical- trial preferred. liver-directed therapy (radioembolization, hepatic arterial infusion melphalan via percutaneous hepatic perfusion - hepzato) where disease is liver-dominant. - adjuvant after enucleation / brachytherapy: no standard adjuvant (sunitinib, dacarbazine, ici all negative in randomized trials); surveillance with q3-6mo liver imaging is the soc. **germline-bap1 caveat:** germline bap1 (bap1 tumor predisposition syndrome) carries lifetime risk of uveal melanoma + mesothelioma + cutaneous melanocytic bap1-inactivated tumors (mbaits) + clear-cell rcc — cascade-test relatives if germline confirmed. **coverage gap acknowledged:** a future dis-uveal entity with its own gnaq / gna11 / cysltr2 driver model and tebentafusp algorithm is the proper home for uveal-specific decision-tree branching. this rf is a stop-gap surfacing the bap1-loss prognostic + tebentafusp- testing-prompt pending that work. uveal (intraokular — choroidal, ziliarkörper, iris) melanom mit somatischem bap1-verlust...  disease: dis-melanoma | sources: src-civic, src-nccn-melanoma-2025 | reviewed 2026-04-29 | pending_clinical_signoff warnhinweis

entries.title: Brustkrebs (invasiv) · Linie 2 · Talazoparib Monotherapie (gBRCA-mutant HER2- lokal fortgeschrittene oder metastasierende Brust)
entries.subtitle: disease: DIS-BREAST | sources: SRC-EMBRACA-LITTON-2018, SRC-ESMO-BREAST-METASTATIC-2024, SRC-NCCN-BREAST-2025 | reviewed 2026-04-29 | pending_clinical_signoff
entries.search_text: ind-breast-brca-met-talazoparib breast cancer (invasive) · line 2 · talazoparib monotherapy (gbrca-mutant her2- locally advanced or metastatic breast) indication indication  src-embraca-litton-2018 src-esmo-breast-metastatic-2024 src-nccn-breast-2025 dis-breast    embraca (nct01945775): phase iii, gbrca1/2-mutant her2- locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer (≤3 prior cytotoxic regimens for advanced disease). talazoparib 1 mg po daily vs physician's- choice single-agent chemo. median pfs 8.6 vs 5.6 mo (hr 0.54); orr 62.6% vs 27.2%. os not significantly different at final analysis (hr 0.85, p=0.17). fda approval oct 2018. this indication is the hr+/her2- brca-mut variant; tnbc variant is ind-breast-tnbc -2l-brca-talazoparib. olaparib olympiad (pfs 7.0 vs 4.2 mo, hr 0.58) is overlapping option; selection driven by ae profile — talazoparib has higher anemia / transfusion burden (~39% g≥3 vs ~16% with olaparib) but greater parp-trapping potency. pre-start: germline brca1/2 panel (peripheral blood) confirmed pathogenic/likely-pathogenic. ua access: talazoparib registered; nszu does not cover for breast — out-of-pocket. brustkrebs (invasiv) · linie 2 · talazoparib monotherapie (gbrca-mutant her2- lokal fortgeschrittene oder metastasierende brust)  disease: dis-breast | sources: src-embraca-litton-2018, src-esmo-breast-metastatic-2024, src-nccn-breast-2025 | reviewed 2026-04-29 | pending_clinical_signoff anwendungsgebiet

entries.search_text: ind-breast-her2-low-2l-dato-dxd breast cancer (invasive) · line 2 · datopotamab deruxtecan (dato-dxd) monotherapy (hr+/her2- pre-treated metastatic post-et + chemo) indication indication  src-esmo-breast-metastatic-2024 src-nccn-breast-2025 dis-breast    aggressive-track. for hr+/her2-low patients who progressed on t-dxd (destiny-breast04 standard 2l) — dato-dxd as 3l+ adc option in her2-low context per tropion-breast01 broad-eligibility design. standard-track 2l for her2-low remains t-dxd (ind-breast-hr-pos-2l -t-dxd-her2-low): pfs 10.1 vs 5.4 mo hr 0.51, os 23.9 vs 17.5 mo hr 0.64. dato-dxd pfs benefit (6.9 vs 4.9 mo, hr 0.63) is smaller in magnitude. sequencing rationale: distinct adc payload (dato-dxd is trop2-targeted, t-dxd is her2-targeted) but shared deruxtecan topo-i-inhibitor warhead — cross-resistance plausible. bibliographic record src-tropion-breast01-bardia-2024 is available; clinical claim linkage requires dual clinical sign-off. ua access: dato-dxd not registered; named-patient import / eap only. brustkrebs (invasiv) · linie 2 · datopotamab deruxtecan (dato-dxd) monotherapie (hr+/her2- vorbehandelte metastasierende post-et + chemo)  disease: dis-breast | sources: src-esmo-breast-metastatic-2024, src-nccn-breast-2025 | reviewed 2026-04-29 | pending_clinical_signoff anwendungsgebiet

entries.search_text: ind-breast-her2-pos-3l-tucatinib breast cancer (invasive) · tucatinib + trastuzumab + capecitabine (her2+ metastatic ≥3l, especially with brain metastases) indication indication  src-esmo-breast-metastatic-2024 src-her2climb-murthy-2019 src-nccn-breast-2025 dis-breast    escat ia. her2climb established tucatinib + trastuzumab + capecitabine for her2+ metastatic ≥3l (post-trastuzumab + post-t-dxd in current era). major unmet need addressed: active brain metastases — first regimen with prospectively-demonstrated intracranial activity. cns-pfs doubling justifies preferred positioning when brain mets present (active or treated). mri brain required pre-treatment to characterize cns disease. diarrhea management dominant clinical workflow burden — combined effect of tucatinib + capecitabine. ua access barrier: tucatinib not registered; named-patient import / eap only. t-dm1 remains an alternative when tucatinib not accessible (katherine / emilia data — not modeled in this batch). breast cancer (invasive) · tucatinib + trastuzumab + capecitabine (her2+ metastatic ≥3l, especially with brain metastases)  disease: dis-breast | sources: src-esmo-breast-metastatic-2024, src-her2climb-murthy-2019, src-nccn-breast-2025 | reviewed 2026-04-27 | pending_clinical_signoff anwendungsgebiet

entries.search_text: ind-breast-hr-pos-2l-akt-capivasertib breast cancer (invasive) · line 2 · capivasertib + fulvestrant (hr+/her2- pik3ca/akt1/pten-altered metastatic post-ai/cdk4/6i) indication indication  src-capitello291-turner-2023 src-esmo-breast-metastatic-2024 src-nccn-breast-2025 dis-breast    escat ia. capitello-291 established capivasertib + fulvestrant for hr+/her2- with pik3ca / akt1 / pten alteration after ai ± cdk4/6i progression. broader biomarker coverage than alpelisib (which gates only on pik3ca): pathway-altered cohort enriched ~41% of itt. diarrhea (72%) management dominant workflow burden — loperamide on hand from day 1, intermittent 4-on/3-off dosing intentionally improves tolerability. ua access barrier: capivasertib not yet registered; named-patient import / eap only. pten-loss definition operationally requires combined ihc + ngs (per capitello enrolment criteria). when both pik3ca-mut and akt1/pten coexist, capivasertib is preferred over alpelisib for pathway-spectrum coverage and intermittent-dosing tolerability. brustkrebs (invasiv) · linie 2 · capivasertib + fulvestrant (hr+/her2- pik3ca/akt1/pten-veränderte metastasierende post-ai/cdk4/6i)  disease: dis-breast | sources: src-capitello291-turner-2023, src-esmo-breast-metastatic-2024, src-nccn-breast-2025 | reviewed 2026-04-27 | pending_clinical_signoff anwendungsgebiet

entries.search_text: ind-breast-hr-pos-2l-dato-dxd breast cancer (invasive) · line 2 · datopotamab deruxtecan (dato-dxd) monotherapy (hr+/her2- pre-treated metastatic post-et + chemo) indication indication  src-esmo-breast-metastatic-2024 src-nccn-breast-2025 dis-breast    tropion-breast01 (nct05104866): phase iii, hr+/her2- metastatic breast post-et + 1-2 prior chemo lines. datopotamab deruxtecan (dato-dxd) 6 mg/kg q3w vs investigator-choice chemo (eribulin / vinorelbine / gemcitabine / capecitabine). median pfs 6.9 vs 4.9 mo (hr 0.63). fda approval jan 2025 (datroway). distinguishing ae profile vs t-dxd: higher stomatitis + ocular toxicity, lower (~3% vs ~12%) ild rate. trop2-ihc not required as predictive biomarker per current label (broad-eligibility design). when her2-low ihc 1+ / 2+ ish- coexists, t-dxd (destiny-breast04 pfs 10.1 vs 5.4 mo, hr 0.51) is preferred over dato-dxd by efficacy margin; dato-dxd is the option for ihc-0 (her2-zero) patients ineligible for t-dxd. bibliographic record src-tropion-breast01-bardia-2024 is available; clinical claim linkage requires dual clinical sign-off. ua access: not registered; named-patient import / eap only. brustkrebs (invasiv) · linie 2 · datopotamab deruxtecan (dato-dxd) monotherapie (hr+/her2- vorbehandelte metastasierende post-et + chemo)  disease: dis-breast | sources: src-esmo-breast-metastatic-2024, src-nccn-breast-2025 | reviewed 2026-04-29 | pending_clinical_signoff anwendungsgebiet

entries.search_text: ind-breast-hr-pos-2l-esr1-elacestrant breast cancer (invasive) · line 2 · elacestrant monotherapy (hr+/her2- esr1-mutant metastatic post-ai/cdk4/6i) indication indication  src-emerald-bidard-2022 src-esmo-breast-metastatic-2024 src-nccn-breast-2025 dis-breast    escat ia. emerald established elacestrant (oral serd) for esr1-mutant hr+/her2- after ai ± cdk4/6i progression. esr1 mutations are acquired on ai therapy (~30-40% of post-ai metastatic) and predict ai resistance — ctdna testing at progression is the preferred detection method (subclonal, polyclonal in tissue). modest absolute pfs gain in overall esr1-mut cohort (3.8 vs 1.9 mo) but enriched in long-cdk4/6i-exposed subgroup. other oral serds (camizestrant, giredestrant, imlunestrant) and protacs (vepdegestrant) in late development. ua access barrier: elacestrant not registered; named-patient import / eap / cross-border only. breast cancer (invasive) · line 2 · elacestrant monotherapy (hr+/her2- esr1-mutant metastatic post-ai/cdk4/6i)  disease: dis-breast | sources: src-emerald-bidard-2022, src-esmo-breast-metastatic-2024, src-nccn-breast-2025 | reviewed 2026-04-27 | pending_clinical_signoff anwendungsgebiet

entries.search_text: ind-breast-hr-pos-2l-ful-everolimus breast cancer (invasive) · line 2 · fulvestrant + everolimus (hr+/her2- metastatic post-ai/cdk4/6i, no targetable mutation) indication indication  src-bolero2-baselga-2012 src-esmo-breast-metastatic-2024 src-nccn-breast-2025 dis-breast    escat ib (no biomarker gating; broad applicability). default 2l hr+/her2- when no targetable mutation found (no pik3ca / akt1 / pten alteration → no capivasertib/alpelisib; no esr1 mutation → no elacestrant) and her2-low not actionable / t-dxd not available. pivotal trial bolero-2 used everolimus + exemestane; precog 0102 validated fulvestrant substitution (mechanistically equivalent; preferred when fulvestrant already in use). stomatitis prophylaxis with dexamethasone mouthwash (swish) reduces g2+ stomatitis from ~33% to ~2% — mandatory pre-medication. pneumonitis (~16% any grade) and immunosuppression-related infections require monitoring. ua access: everolimus registered (generics + brand afinitor) but nszu does not cover breast indication — out-of-pocket; generic substantially cheaper. brustkrebs (invasiv) · linie 2 · fulvestrant + everolimus (hr+/her2- metastasiert nach der ki/cdk4/6i, keine zielfähige mutation)  disease: dis-breast | sources: src-bolero2-baselga-2012, src-esmo-breast-metastatic-2024, src-nccn-breast-2025 | reviewed 2026-04-27 | pending_clinical_signoff anwendungsgebiet

entries.search_text: ind-breast-tnbc-2l-t-dxd-her2-low breast cancer (invasive) · line 2 · t-dxd monotherapy (her2+ metastatic 2l+, also her2-low metastatic) indication indication  src-destiny-breast04-modi-2022 src-esmo-breast-metastatic-2024 src-nccn-breast-2025 dis-breast    escat ia. destiny-breast04 included a small tnbc her2-low cohort (n=63) with consistent benefit signal — t-dxd should be preferred over sacituzumab when her2-low confirmed (ihc 1+ or ihc 2+/ish-). when her2-ihc = 0, sacituzumab govitecan (ascent) is the default ≥2l. ild risk dominant safety concern — baseline ct chest + active monitoring. ua access barrier: t-dxd registered but reimbursement under negotiation. sequencing question (t-dxd then sacituzumab vs reverse) is unsettled; algo-breast-tnbc-2l defaults to t-dxd-first for her2-low. brustkrebs (invasiv) · linie 2 · t-dxd monotherapie (her2+ metastasiert 2l+, auch her2-low metastasiert)  disease: dis-breast | sources: src-destiny-breast04-modi-2022, src-esmo-breast-metastatic-2024, src-nccn-breast-2025 | reviewed 2026-04-27 | pending_clinical_signoff anwendungsgebiet

entries.search_text: ind-mesothelioma-1l-nivo-ipi malignant pleural mesothelioma (mpm) · line 1 · nivolumab + ipilimumab (mesothelioma, 1l) indication indication  src-checkmate-743-baas-2021 src-nccn-nsclc-2025 dis-mesothelioma    checkmate-743 (pmid 33581810) is the landmark mpm 1l trial. fda approved october 2020 for unresectable mpm — first new 1l approval in 15 years. histology-driven routing is essential: non-epithelioid mpm derives far greater benefit (hr 0.46) and nivo+ipi should be strongly preferred; epithelioid still benefits (hr 0.86) but chemotherapy remains an alternative. sources note: mpm is sometimes managed by thoracic oncologists who may reference nccn mesothelioma guidelines (separate from nsclc). src-nccn-nsclc-2025 used as proxy — dedicated nccn mesothelioma source should be added. malignes pleuramesotheliom (mpm) · linie 1 · nivolumab + ipilimumab (mesoteliom, 1l)  disease: dis-mesothelioma | sources: src-checkmate-743-baas-2021, src-nccn-nsclc-2025 | reviewed 2026-05-04 | pending_clinical_signoff anwendungsgebiet

entries.search_text: ind-mesothelioma-2l-nivo malignant pleural mesothelioma (mpm) · line 2 · nivolumab monotherapy (mesothelioma 2l, confirm) indication indication  src-confirm-fennell-2021 src-nccn-nsclc-2025 dis-mesothelioma    confirm (pmid 34090562) is the first phase-3 rct with os benefit for 2l mpm. first platinum-based therapy was pemetrexed+cisplatin/carboplatin in most patients. nivolumab benefit observed in both epithelioid (majority of patients) and non-epithelioid subtypes — distinct from the 1l checkmate-743 pattern where non-epithelioid derived substantially greater benefit. pd-l1 expression status is not required for patient selection; confirm enrolled an unselected population and os benefit was consistent across pd-l1 subgroups. active autoimmune disease, prior organ transplantation, and ongoing corticosteroids >10 mg/d prednisone equivalent are clinical contraindications (not kb entity ids — hard_contraindications remains []). nccn source note: mpm is managed under a dedicated nccn mesothelioma guideline separate from nsclc. src-nccn-nsclc-2025 is used as proxy here (same approach as ind-mesothelioma-1l-nivo-ipi). a dedicated nccn mesothelioma source should be added when available. malignes pleuramesotheliom (mpm) · linie 2 · nivolumab monotherapie (mesoteliom 2l, confirm)  disease: dis-mesothelioma | sources: src-confirm-fennell-2021, src-nccn-nsclc-2025 | reviewed 2026-05-07 | pending_clinical_signoff anwendungsgebiet

entries.search_text: ind-mm-1l-dara-rd multiple myeloma · line 1 · daratumumab + lenalidomide + dexamethasone (d-rd, maia — mm 1l transplant-ineligible) indication indication  src-maia-facon-2019 src-nccn-mm-2025 dis-mm    stub — requires clinical co-lead signoff before publication. aggressive counterpart to ind-mm-1l-rd for two-plan output in transplant-ineligible ndmm (charter §2). major access constraint in ukraine: daratumumab is not currently нсзу-reimbursed — funding pathway (clinical trial / charitable / out-of-pocket) must be confirmed before this plan is finalized. red-cell phenotyping (type and screen) before first daratumumab dose is mandatory due to anti-cd38 interference with crossmatching. maia trial (facon nejm 2019, pmid 30926586): 737 transplant-ineligible ndmm patients randomized d-rd vs rd. primary endpoint pfs: hr 0.56 (95% ci 0.43–0.73), p<0.001. 5-year os update (facon jco 2024): 66.3% vs 53.1% (hr 0.66, p<0.0001) — first os benefit for an anti-cd38 doublet addition in ti-ndmm. scope gate: fit_for_transplant: false restricts ind-mm-1l-dara-rd to transplant-ineligible patients. for transplant-eligible aggressive-plan patients, see ind-mm-1l-dvrd (d-vrd + asct + dara-len maintenance). treatment is continuous until progression or unacceptable toxicity — no fixed-duration transplant pathway. no phases block needed (single continuous regimen, no asct step). multiple myeloma · line 1 · daratumumab + lenalidomide + dexamethasone (d-rd, maia — mm 1l transplant-ineligible)  disease: dis-mm | sources: src-maia-facon-2019, src-nccn-mm-2025 | reviewed 2026-05-09 | pending_clinical_signoff anwendungsgebiet

entries.subtitle: disease: DIS-NSCLC | sources: SRC-CHECKMATE-9LA-PAZ-ARES-2021, SRC-ESMO-NSCLC-METASTATIC-2024, SRC-NCCN-NSCLC-2025 | reviewed 2026-05-07
entries.search_text: ind-nsclc-driver-neg-met-1l-nivo-ipi-chemo non-small cell lung cancer · line 1 · nivolumab + ipilimumab + 2-cycle platinum-doublet chemotherapy (checkmate-9la) indication indication  src-checkmate-9la-paz-ares-2021 src-esmo-nsclc-metastatic-2024 src-nccn-nsclc-2025 dis-nsclc    checkmate-9la (paz-ares 2021, lancet oncol; nct03215706): phase iii rct, 719 patients, driver-negative stage iv nsclc, any pd-l1 tps. nivo 360 mg q3w + ipi 1 mg/kg q6w + 2 cycles platinum-doublet chemo vs 4 cycles platinum-doublet chemo alone. key clinical differentiation: - vs checkmate-227 (nivo+ipi alone, any pd-l1): addition of 2 chemo cycles provides faster early disease control and higher early orr; especially advantageous for symptomatic disease, large burden, or when rapid response is needed. - vs keynote-189/nivo+chemo: dual-io backbone (nivo+ipi) with chemotherapy provides durable long-tail os benefit (3-year os 25% vs 14%) not seen with pd-1 mono + chemo. - pd-l1 subgroup analysis: os benefit consistent across tps <1% (hr 0.62), tps 1–49% (hr 0.79), tps ≥50% (hr 0.66) — regimen is pd-l1 agnostic. patient selection: driver-negative stage iv nsclc is confirmed only after negative comprehensive molecular profiling (ngs panel). pd-l1 testing required to document eligibility but does not stratify treatment in this indication. chemotherapy component: only 2 cycles administered. histology-specific selection: squamous → carboplatin auc 6 + paclitaxel; non-squamous → carboplatin auc 5 + pemetrexed. after 2 cycles, io doublet (nivo+ipi) continues alone. note: bio-kras-g12c, bio-met-ex14, bio-braf-v600e, bio-ret-fusion, bio-ntrk-fusion exclusion is captured as clinical prose above; only bio-egfr-mutation and bio-alk-fusion are listed in biomarker_requirements_excluded as those bio-* ids are confirmed in kb. other driver biomarker exclusions documented in stage_requirements prose. non-small cell lung cancer · line 1 · nivolumab + ipilimumab + 2-cycle platinum-doublet chemotherapy (checkmate-9la)  disease: dis-nsclc | sources: src-checkmate-9la-paz-ares-2021, src-esmo-nsclc-metastatic-2024, src-nccn-nsclc-2025 | reviewed 2026-05-07 anwendungsgebiet

primary citations route through src-nccn-pancreatic-2025 and src-esmo-pancreatic-2024 which themselves cite both trials and carry the consensus-recommendation evidence chain. future chunk should author the lap07-hammel-2016 and conko-007-fietkau-2022 source stubs and back-fill direct citations into rationale and rc notes. evidence-level moderate + strength conditional + nccn 2a: lap07 was os-negative; entries.search_text: ind-sclc-rr-tarlatamab small cell lung cancer · line 2 · tarlatamab — 2l+ extensive-stage sclc (dellphi-301; dll3 × cd3 bite) indication indication  src-dellphi-301-ahn-2023 src-esmo-sclc-2021 src-nccn-sclc-2025 dis-sclc    stub — pending clinical co-lead sign-off. aggressive-track 2l for r/r es-sclc after platinum-based 1l chemotherapy. no biomarker dependency for label use (dll3 ihc not required); applicability driven by line-of-therapy + ecog + organ function + access to inpatient infusion centre. mandatory cycle 1 inpatient monitoring (≥22 hr post d1 + d8) + tocilizumab-on-formulary + icu access for grade ≥3 crs are structural deployment constraints beyond drug acquisition cost. ukraine access constraint dominant (not registered, not нсзу; out-of-pocket usd 30-40k/cycle) and structural infrastructure barrier limits realistic deployment. evidence level: moderate (single-arm phase 2 + fda accelerated approval; phase 3 dellphi-304 confirmatory trial pending); strength of recommendation: conditional. algorithm wiring deferred — sclc r/r algorithm not yet authored in kb; out of chunk scope. pul-a4 chunk closes #491. kleinzell-lungenkrebs · linie 2 · tarlatamab — 2l+ extensive sclc (dellphi-301; dll3 × cd3 bite)  disease: dis-sclc | sources: src-dellphi-301-ahn-2023, src-esmo-sclc-2021, src-nccn-sclc-2025 | reviewed 2026-05-08 | pending_clinical_signoff | actionability review required anwendungsgebiet

entries.search_text: reg-cinv-4drug-hec 4-drug cinv prophylaxis (high-emetogenic chemo: nk1 + 5ht3 + dex + olanzapine) regimen regimen  src-esmo-aml-2020 src-nccn-aml-2025     mascc/esmo 2016 + nccn antiemesis 2025 standard for high-emetogenic chemo (hec = cisplatin ≥50 mg/m², ac, carboplatin auc ≥4 (since 2017), cyclophosphamide ≥1500 mg/m², hd-cytarabine, others). full 4-drug: (1) nk1 antagonist — aprepitant 125 mg po day 1, 80 mg po days 2-3 (or fosaprepitant 150 mg iv day 1 single dose; or nepa combination netupitant-palonosetron 300/0.5 mg po day 1 single); (2) 5ht3 antagonist — palonosetron 0.25 mg iv day 1 preferred (single-dose covers acute + delayed) or ondansetron 8 mg iv / 16 mg po; (3) dexamethasone 12 mg day 1 with nk1 (or 20 mg without nk1), then 8 mg daily days 2-4; (4) olanzapine 10 mg po qhs days 1-4 (prond trial navari 2017 nejm — added to triplet, ~50% reduction in cinv failure). olanzapine also substitutes for delayed-phase dexamethasone (steroid-sparing). for ukraine where aprepitant unavailable, the best evidence-based alternative is ondansetron + dexamethasone + olanzapine triplet (nccn supports this combination for hec when nk1 unavailable). drug ids missing in kb and to be authored: nk1 agents (aprepitant/fosaprepitant/rolapitant/netupitant), olanzapine, palonosetron, metoclopramide, lorazepam — flagged for prod batch. 4-drug cinv prophylaxis (high-emetogenic chemo: nk1 + 5ht3 + dex + olanzapine)  sources: src-esmo-aml-2020, src-nccn-aml-2025 | reviewed 2026-04-27 | pending_clinical_signoff therapieschema

entries.search_text: reg-5fu-lv-bev-ckd-modified 5-fu + leucovorin + bevacizumab (slv5fu2-bev, crc severe ckd crcl <30 — oxali/cape unsafe) regimen regimen  src-esmo-colon-2024 src-nccn-colon-2025     capecitabine is contraindicated crcl <30 (renally cleared, severe toxicity risk). oxaliplatin is hepatically cleared but has additive nephrotoxicity in pre-existing ckd; risk-benefit unfavourable in severe ckd where neuropathy is also harder to manage. slv5fu2-bev (simplified bolus + 46h civi 5-fu + leucovorin + bev) provides a reasonable backbone for mcrc in severe ckd when chemo is still desired. 5-fu is hepatically metabolised (dpd); no dose adjustment needed for renal impairment (parent and metabolites only ~5-10% renal). bevacizumab dose reduced to 5 mg/kg q2w (vs standard 5-7.5 mg/kg q2w) to limit proteinuria worsening; close bp + upc monitoring. dpyd pre-screening strongly recommended (cpic). 5-fu + leucovorin + bevacizumab (slv5fu2-bev, crc schwere ckd crcl < 30 — oxali/cape unsicher)  sources: src-esmo-colon-2024, src-nccn-colon-2025 | reviewed 2026-04-27 | pending_clinical_signoff therapieschema

entries.search_text: reg-aml-7-3-go 7+3 + fractionated gemtuzumab ozogamicin (cd33+ aml, 1l; alfa-0701) regimen regimen  src-alfa-0701-castaigne-2012 src-eln-aml-2022 src-nccn-aml-2025     alfa-0701 (castaigne lancet 2012): fractionated go 3 mg/m² days 1, 4, 7 added to standard 7+3 in 1l de-novo aml age 50-70. 2-yr efs 40.8% vs 17.1% (hr 0.58); 2-yr os 53.2% vs 41.9% (hr 0.69). hills meta-analysis 2014 (lancet oncol): go addition reduces 5-yr mortality by ~20% in favorable-risk (hr 0.47) and intermediate-risk (hr 0.84); no benefit in adverse-risk (hr 1.03). aml-19 (burnett 2017) supports go 6 mg/m² single dose in elderly unfit-for-7+3 but is a different regimen entity. position: preferred 1l for fit cd33+ cbf / favorable / intermediate- risk aml where go accessible. daunorubicin dose 60 mg/m² (not 90) when adding go due to additive cardiotoxicity. hepatic vod/sos is the dominant safety concern — careful lft monitoring + allohct timing (avoid go within 90 days of planned allohct). 7+3 + fraktioniert gemtuzumab ozogamicin (cd33+ aml, 1l; alfa-0701)  sources: src-alfa-0701-castaigne-2012, src-eln-aml-2022, src-nccn-aml-2025 | reviewed 2026-04-30 | pending_clinical_signoff therapieschema

entries.title: Bemarituzumab + mFOLFOX6 (FORTITUDE-101) — 1L FGFR2b-overexpressing HER2-non-positive gastric/GEJ
entries.subtitle: sources: SRC-ESMO-GASTRIC-2024, SRC-FIGHT, SRC-FORTITUDE-101, SRC-NCCN-GASTRIC-2025 | reviewed 2026-05-07 | pending_clinical_signoff
entries.search_text: reg-bemarituzumab-mfolfox6 bemarituzumab + mfolfox6 (fortitude-101) — 1l fgfr2b-overexpressing her2-non-positive gastric/gej regimen regimen  src-esmo-gastric-2024 src-fight src-fortitude-101 src-nccn-gastric-2025     fortitude-101 (rha et al. esmo 2025 lba10; nct05052801) phase 3 registrational: bemarituzumab + mfolfox6 vs placebo + mfolfox6 in fgfr2b-overexpressing (ihc 2+/3+ ≥10% of tumor cells, validated iiib-selective antibody) her2-non-positive 1l unresectable / metastatic gastric/gej adenocarcinoma. primary analysis (median follow-up 11.8 mo): mos 17.9 vs 12.5 mo (hr 0.61, p=0.005); mpfs 8.6 vs 6.7 mo (hr 0.71, 95% ci 0.53–0.95); orr ~45% in both arms. updated descriptive analysis (median follow-up 19.4 mo): mos 14.5 vs 13.2 mo (hr 0.82, 95% ci 0.62–1.08) — early survival gain attenuated with longer follow-up, raising practice-changing controversy at esmo 2025 (one discussant characterized the data as "biologic activity, not practice-changing" citing absence of pd-1 backbone in control arm and shrinking median os difference). predecessor fight phase 2 (wainberg et al. lancet oncol 2022) showed mpfs 9.5 vs 7.4 mo (hr 0.68) in the same fgfr2b ≥10% 2+/3+ subgroup. ocular toxicity is the dose-defining ae: ~70% any-grade corneal events (punctate keratitis, reduced visual acuity, dry eye, corneal epithelium defect), ~25% grade ≥3, 28% withdrawal due to ocular toxicity (typical onset ~6 months) — mandatory baseline + serial slit-lamp ophthalmology required. bemarituzumab dosing per fortitude-101 protocol: 15 mg/kg iv q2w with cycle 1 day 8 additional 7.5 mg/kg loading dose. hierarchy when multiple actionable signals co-occur in her2-non-positive 1l gastric/gej: her2+ trastuzumab supersedes; msi-h pembrolizumab supersedes; cldn18.2 ≥75% zolbetuximab supersedes (phase 3 os established oct 2024 vs fortitude-101 attenuated benefit); bemarituzumab reserved for fgfr2b ≥10% with cldn18.2 <75%. stub pending clinical co-lead sign-off (charter §6.1: ≥2 reviewers for clinical content). drug-bemarituzumab entity does not yet exist in kb — drug-stub creation deferred to a separate chunk; transient ref-error expected until then. bemarituzumab + mfolfox6 (fortitude-101) — 1l fgfr2b-overexpressing her2-non-positive gastric/gej  sources: src-esmo-gastric-2024, src-fight, src-fortitude-101, src-nccn-gastric-2025 | reviewed 2026-05-07 | pending_clinical_signoff therapieschema

entries.search_text: reg-cabozantinib-mtc-1l cabozantinib monotherapy (advanced/progressive ret-wt mtc, 1l; or ret-mutant where ret-selective unavailable) regimen regimen  src-nccn-thyroid-2025     exam (schoffski 2012): cabozantinib 140 mg vs placebo improved pfs 11.2 vs 4.0 mo in advanced progressive mtc; os benefit in ret m918t subgroup (hr 0.60). default 1l for ret-wt mtc (ras-mutant or unknown — no ret-selective option) and a fallback for ret-mutant mtc if selpercatinib / pralsetinib are inaccessible. vandetanib (zeta) is the alternative multikinase mtc tki; both predate the ret-selective era and carry substantial toxicity (hfsr, gi perforation, hypertension, hemorrhage, onj). cometriq capsules (mtc) and cabometyx tablets (rcc/hcc/dtc) are not bioequivalent — do not substitute. cabozantinib monotherapy (advanced/progressive ret-wt mtc, 1l; or ret-mutant where ret-selective unavailable)  quellen: src-nccn-thyroid-2025-bewertet 2026-04-27-- bis zum klinischen_signoff therapieschema

entries.search_text: reg-capecitabine-palliative capecitabine palliative monotherapy (crc ecog 3-4, bsc-adjacent low-intensity) regimen regimen  src-esmo-colon-2024 src-nccn-colon-2025     in ecog 3-4 mcrc patients where full doublet (folfox/capox) or triplet (folfirinox) is not feasible due to performance status, comorbidity burden, or patient preference, single-agent capecitabine offers a low-toxicity oral option that preserves quality of life while providing modest disease control (mpfs ~4-6 mo in unselected populations; longer in mss / well-differentiated tumours). avoids iv access requirements and reduces clinic burden. discuss explicitly with patient + family that the goal is symptom-balance, not life-prolongation in any meaningful sense — this regimen is bsc-adjacent and the boundary between treatment and bsc is fluid. co-enrol palliative care early. dpyd pre-screening strongly recommended (cpic) — dpyd deficiency causes severe-fatal toxicity. capecitabine palliative monotherapy (crc ecog 3-4, bsc-adjacent low-intensity)  sources: src-esmo-colon-2024, src-nccn-colon-2025 | reviewed 2026-04-27 | pending_clinical_signoff therapieschema

entries.search_text: reg-carboplatin-paclitaxel-gct carboplatin + paclitaxel (adult granulosa cell tumor, advanced/recurrent) regimen regimen  src-esmo-ovarian-2024 src-nccn-ovarian-2025     carboplatin + paclitaxel is widely used as first-line chemotherapy for advanced/recurrent adult granulosa cell tumor (agct), extrapolated from ovarian cancer chemotherapy practice. no large randomized trial specific to gct. bep (bleomycin-etoposide-cisplatin) is an alternative (especially in younger patients or when platinum-taxane sensitivity unknown). response rates ~50–70% in recurrent disease. surgery remains primary modality; chemo is for advanced/inoperable or chemotherapy-sensitive recurrence. hormone-directed therapy (leuprolide, letrozole) is active in hormone receptor-positive gct, especially for maintenance. carboplatin + paclitaxel (erwachsener granulosa-zelltumor, fortgeschritten/rezidivierend)  sources: src-esmo-ovarian-2024, src-nccn-ovarian-2025 | reviewed 2026-05-04 | pending_clinical_signoff therapieschema

entries.title: Ciltacabtagene autoleucel (cilta-cel) BCMA CAR-T for lenalidomide-refractory R/R multiple myeloma after 1-3 prior lines — single infusion after Flu/Cy lymphodepletion (CARTITUDE-4)
entries.subtitle: sources: SRC-CARTITUDE-1-BERDEJA-2021, SRC-NCCN-MM-2025 | reviewed 2026-04-29 | pending_clinical_signoff
entries.search_text: reg-ciltacel-mm-2l ciltacabtagene autoleucel (cilta-cel) bcma car-t for lenalidomide-refractory r/r multiple myeloma after 1-3 prior lines — single infusion after flu/cy lymphodepletion (cartitude-4) regimen regimen  src-cartitude-1-berdeja-2021 src-nccn-mm-2025     cartitude-4 (nct04181827, san-miguel nejm 2023, pmid 37272512): randomized phase-3 of single-infusion cilta-cel vs investigator's choice (pvd or dpd) in lenalidomide-refractory r/r multiple myeloma after 1-3 prior lines (n=419, 1:1 randomization). cilta-cel arm: orr 84.6%, scr 73.1%; mpfs not reached vs 11.8 mo control (hr 0.26, p<0.001); 12-mo pfs 75.9% vs 48.6%. established cilta-cel as superior to standard-of-care triplets in lenalidomide-refractory 2l+ mm. fda approval apr 2024 (this 2l indication). mnt mitigation strategies (low tumor burden via bridging, prompt crs/icans rx) reduced delayed-onset neurotoxicity from ~5% (cartitude-1) to ~1% (cartitude-4). centre must be fact/jacie/rems-accredited. boxed warnings unchanged from cartitude-1 (crs, icans, mnt, hlh/mas, prolonged cytopenia, secondary t-cell malignancy). single curative-intent attempt; no maintenance. stub — pending co-lead sign-off. bibliographic record src-cartitude-4-san-miguel-2023 (nejm pmid 37272512) is available; source-to-claim mapping, including trial-design and safety context, requires dual clinical review. ciltacabtagene autoleucel (cilta-cel) bcma car-t for lenalidomide-refractory r/r multiple myeloma after 1-3 prior lines — single infusion after flu/cy lymphodepletion (cartitude-4)  sources: src-cartitude-1-berdeja-2021, src-nccn-mm-2025 | reviewed 2026-04-29 | pending_clinical_signoff therapieschema

entries.title: Concurrent capecitabine radiosensitization (825 mg/m² PO BID on RT days only) — paired with conventionally fractionated GI chemoradiation
entries.subtitle: sources: SRC-ESMO-CRC-2024, SRC-NCCN-COLON-2025, SRC-NCCN-PANCREATIC-2025, SRC-PRODIGE-23-CONROY-2021 | reviewed 2026-05-08 | pending_clinical_signoff | actionability review required
entries.search_text: reg-capecitabine-crt-concurrent concurrent capecitabine radiosensitization (825 mg/m² po bid on rt days only) — paired with conventionally fractionated gi chemoradiation regimen regimen  src-esmo-crc-2024 src-nccn-colon-2025 src-nccn-pancreatic-2025 src-prodige-23-conroy-2021     concurrent radiosensitizing capecitabine paired with a conventionally fractionated gi radiationcourse — distinct from the cyclic palliative capecitabine pattern (reg-capecitabine-palliative: 1000 mg/m² bid days 1-14 / 21d for ecog 3-4 mcrc). the 825 mg/m² po bid "on rt days only" schedule has no fixed cycle structure: capecitabine is taken monday through friday during each week of rt delivery (with the daily dose split bid, typically ~12 hours apart, ideally bracketing the rt fraction), held on weekends and any rt-off days, and stopped with the final rt fraction. total exposure ~5.5 weeks for the canonical 50.4 gy / 28 fx pairing. authored to back-fill the `concurrent_chemo_regimen` fk on two §17 radiationcourse entities that previously had to leave the field explicitly null with audit-trail comments because no matching regimen existed: - rc-lccrt-504-28-rectal — long-course preoperative chemoradiation for locally advanced rectal cancer (prodige-23 tnt crt phase / standard arm; src-prodige-23-conroy-2021, src-nccn-colon-2025, src-esmo-crc-2024). conroy 2021, lancet oncology n=461; 3-yr dfs 75.7% (tnt) vs 68.5% (standard); pcr 27.8% vs 12.1%. - rc-lapc-chemoradiation-pdac — definitive consolidation chemoradiation for locally advanced unresectable pancreatic adenocarcinoma (nccn-pancreatic v.4.2025 preferred concurrent regimen; src-nccn-pancreatic-2025). sequenced after ~6 cycles of induction folfirinox/mfolfirinox in patients without progression. hofheinz 2012 (lancet oncology) established capecitabine non-inferiority to infusional 5-fu 225 mg/m²/day civ in rectal crt (5-yr os 75.7% cape vs 66.6% 5-fu, p=0.04 favoring cape) and that result generalizes by clinical convention to pancreatic lapc consolidation crt, where nccn-pancreatic v.4.2025 lists capecitabine and infusional 5-fu as interchangeable concurrent radiosensitizers. the infusional 5-fu alternative remains a valid substitute for patients with capecitabine-specific contraindications (severe hfs history, dpyd homozygous deficiency, symptomatic cad with prior 5-fu cardiotoxicity, crcl <30 ml/min where capecitabine is contraindicated but supervised iv 5-fu may be feasible at a reduced dose). toxicity profile: moderate. hand-foot syndrome and diarrhea (rectal) / enteritis (lapc) dominate. proctitis (rectal lccrt) and mucositis / esophagitis / gastritis (lapc, due to stomach/duodenum overlap with the rt field) are rt-driven but capecitabine amplifies them via radiosensitization. rt continuity is the primary local-control driver, so chemo is held in preference to pausing rt whenever possible (capecitabine is the modifiable variable; rt fractionation is fixed). dpyd pre-screening per cpic strongly recommended before starting any fluoropyrimidine-based radiosensitization — dpyd-deficient patients experience severe-fatal mucositis, diarrhea, and myelosuppression even at 50% capecitabine reduction. pairing pattern (canonical §17 radiationcourse fk): rc.concurrent_chemo_regimen → reg-capecitabine-crt-concurrent.id. this regimen is not intended for stand-alone systemic-therapy use; always paired with a radiationcourse entity that defines the rt fractionation, target volume, and total dose. render layer should surface this regimen only in the context of its paired radiationcourse, never as a candidate cyclic chemo regimen. concurrent capecitabine radiosensitization (825 mg/m² po bid on rt days only) — paired with conventionally fractionated gi chemoradiation  sources: src-esmo-crc-2024, src-nccn-colon-2025, src-nccn-pancreatic-2025, src-prodige-23-conroy-2021 | reviewed 2026-05-08 | pending_clinical_signoff | actionability review required therapieschema

entries.title: Daratumumab + Lenalidomide maintenance post-ASCT (PERSEUS schedule)
entries.subtitle: sources: SRC-NCCN-MM-2025, SRC-PERSEUS-SONNEVELD-2024 | reviewed 2026-05-09 | pending_clinical_signoff
entries.search_text: reg-dara-len-maintenance daratumumab + lenalidomide maintenance post-asct (perseus schedule) regimen regimen  src-nccn-mm-2025 src-perseus-sonneveld-2024     perseus maintenance arm (sonneveld nejm 2024, pmid 38084760): after d-vrd × 4 induction + asct + d-vrd × 2 consolidation, patients received daratumumab sc q4w (first 6 cycles then q8w) + lenalidomide 10 mg d1-21 until progression. median maintenance duration ~38 months. distinct from: (1) reg-lenalidomide-maintenance (len-only, no daratumumab — calgb 100104 / ifm 2005-02 schema); (2) mrd-guided approaches (investigational). key perseus maintenance outcomes: 48-month pfs 84.3% (d-vrd arm) vs 67.7% (vrd arm); mrd-negativity (10⁻⁵) at 12 months post-consolidation 75.2% vs 47.5%. the pfs benefit was consistent across transplant-eligible subgroups including high-risk cytogenetics (del17p, t[4;14], t[14;16]). daratumumab dosing transition in perseus: q4w during consolidation and first 6 maintenance cycles → q8w thereafter. some ukrainian centers may default to q4w throughout for simplicity; both schedules are documented. second primary malignancy (spm) risk: the combination of asct + extended lenalidomide increases spm risk (mds/aml ~2-3% at 5 yr, solid tumors). must be included in pre-consent discussion. risk-benefit favors maintenance in standard-risk and high-risk ndmm given the magnitude of pfs gain. red-cell phenotyping before first daratumumab dose is mandatory (anti-cd38 interference with crossmatching) — maintained through maintenance phase; update type-and-screen before each quarterly assessment. daratumumab + lenalidomide maintenance post-asct (perseus schedule)  sources: src-nccn-mm-2025, src-perseus-sonneveld-2024 | reviewed 2026-05-09 | pending_clinical_signoff therapieschema

entries.search_text: regimen-epcoritamab-mono-dlbcl-3l epcoritamab sc monotherapy for r/r dlbcl ≥3l (epcore nhl-1) regimen regimen  src-esmo-dlbcl-2024 src-nccn-bcell-2025     first-in-class subcutaneous cd20×cd3 bispecific t-cell engager for relapsed/refractory diffuse large b-cell lymphoma after ≥2 prior lines (including patients ineligible for or relapsed after car-t). epcore nhl-1 (thieblemont et al., j clin oncol 2023): in r/r lbcl ≥3l (n=157, ~39% prior car-t) — orr ~63%, cr ~39%, median dor ~12 months, median pfs ~4.4 mo, median os not reached at primary analysis. step-up dosing (0.16 → 0.8 → 48 mg) + cycle-1 corticosteroid prophylaxis reduce crs to predominantly grade 1-2 (any-grade ~50%, g≥3 ~3%). icans ~6% any-grade. sc route + ambulatory schedule favourable vs iv bispecifics for outpatient-heavy practices. continuous indefinite dosing (vs 12-cycle fixed-duration glofitamab) is the principal sequencing trade-off. see regimen-epcoritamab-step-up-dosing for the standalone cycle-1 step-up sub-schedule. bibliographic record src-epcore-nhl-1-thieblemont-2023 is available; clinical claim linkage requires dual clinical sign-off. epcoritamab sc monotherapie für r/r dlbcl ≥3l (epcore nhl-1)  sources: src-esmo-dlbcl-2024, src-nccn-bcell-2025 | reviewed 2026-05-01 | pending_clinical_signoff therapieschema

entries.search_text: reg-erdafitinib-urothelial-2l erdafitinib monotherapy (thor cohort 1) — 2l+ fgfr2/3-altered metastatic urothelial carcinoma regimen regimen  src-nccn-bladder-2025     thor (loriot nejm 2023) phase 3, cohort 1: erdafitinib 8 mg po daily (with up-titration to 9 mg if phosphate <5.5 mg/dl day 14) vs investigator-choice chemotherapy (docetaxel or vinflunine) in metastatic urothelial carcinoma with selected fgfr2/3 alterations (mutation s249c / r248c / g370c / y373c or fgfr2/3 fusion), after ≥1 prior line including pd-(l)1 inhibitor (n=266; 136 erda vs 130 chemo). met primary endpoint mos 12.1 vs 7.8 mo (hr 0.64, p=0.005), mpfs 5.6 vs 2.7 mo (hr 0.58), orr 35.3% vs 8.5%. thor cohort 2 (erda vs pembrolizumab in pd-(l)1-naive) was negative and not used to support labeling. fda converted accelerated to full approval jan 2024 based on thor cohort 1. class toxicity: hyperphosphatemia (~76%), nail toxicity (~57%), stomatitis, central serous retinopathy (~25%, usually reversible). stub pending clinical co-lead sign-off. trial source src-thor-loriot-2023 not yet authored in kb; cited via nccn-bladder-2025 (urothelial esmo guideline not yet in kb either — flagged in commit body). erdafitinib-monotherapie (ther-kohorte 1) — 2l+ fgfr2/3-alteriertes metastasierendes urothelkarzinom  quellen: src-nccn-bladder-2025-geprüft 2026-04-29-umgestellt in erwartung_klinisch_signoff therapieschema

entries.search_text: reg-everolimus-exemestane everolimus + exemestane (hr+/her2- breast 3l+, post cdk4/6i and pi3ki/akti) regimen regimen  src-bolero2-baselga-2012 src-esmo-breast-metastatic-2024 src-nccn-breast-2025     bolero-2 (baselga 2012, nejm): everolimus + exemestane vs exemestane alone in hr+ mbc progressing on non-steroidal ai — mpfs 7.8 vs 3.2 mo. now positioned 3l+ in the era of cdk4/6i (1l) and pi3k/akt inhibitors (alpelisib for pik3ca-mut, capivasertib for akt-pathway alterations). stomatitis is dominant toxicity — dexamethasone mouthwash prophylaxis (swish trial, rugo 2017) is mandatory and dramatically reduces g2+ stomatitis. pneumonitis (1-2% g3) requires prompt recognition. useful for endocrine-sensitive disease where cdk4/6i + ai/fulvestrant has failed; alternative to chemo in slowly-progressive er+ mbc. everolimus + exemestane (hr+/her2-mamma 3l+, nach cdk4/6i und pi3ki/akti)  sources: src-bolero2-baselga-2012, src-esmo-breast-metastatic-2024, src-nccn-breast-2025 | reviewed 2026-04-27 | pending_clinical_signoff therapieschema

entries.search_text: reg-everolimus-mono-pnet everolimus monotherapy (advanced/progressive pnet g1/g2; radiant-3) regimen regimen  src-nccn-net-2025 src-radiant3-yao-2011     radiant-3 (yao nejm 2011): everolimus 10 mg/day vs placebo in progressive well-differentiated pnet (n=410). mpfs 11.0 vs 4.6 mo (hr 0.35, p<0.001). no significant os benefit demonstrated (confounded by >70% crossover post- progression). ssa prior / concurrent use allowed. stomatitis prophylaxis (dexamethasone mouthwash, swish trial) reduces g2+ stomatitis dramatically. sunitinib 37.5 mg/day is the alternative (raymond nejm 2011 — similar mpfs 11.4 vs 5.5 mo, hr 0.42); no head-to-head comparison; choice based on comorbidities (cardiac/renal → prefer everolimus; diabetes/steroids → consider sunitinib). stub pending §6.1 signoff. everolimus monotherapie (fortgeschritten/progressiv pnet g1/g2; radiant-3)  sources: src-nccn-net-2025, src-radiant3-yao-2011 | reviewed 2026-05-03 | pending_clinical_signoff therapieschema

entries.title: Exemestane 25 mg täglich × 5 Jahre für postmenopausale Brustkrebschemoprevention

entries.search_text: reg-exemestane-chemoprevention exemestane 25 mg daily × 5 years for postmenopausal breast-cancer chemoprevention regimen regimen  src-nccn-breast-2025     exemestane 25 mg po daily × 5 years for breast-cancer chemoprevention in postmenopausal women only per map.3 (goss 2011, nejm). ~65% reduction in invasive breast cancer with lower endometrial/vte risk than tamoxifen. ibis-ii (cuzick 2014) established similar efficacy for anastrozole. both ais are nccn-endorsed first-line chemoprevention options for postmenopausal high-risk women. bone health monitoring (dxa at baseline + q2 years) is critical — adverse impact on bmd is the main downside vs. raloxifene (which preserves bmd). not for premenopausal use (requires functioning postmenopausal ovary; would not block premenopausal estrogen production). exemestane 25 mg täglich × 5 jahre für postmenopausale brustkrebschemoprevention  quellen: src-nccn-breast-2025-bericht vom 2026-05-18-bericht ausstehender_klinischer_abzeichen therapieschema

entries.search_text: reg-extreme-hnscc extreme (cetuximab + cisplatin/carboplatin + 5-fu; hnscc r/m, 1l) regimen regimen  src-esmo-hnscc-2020 src-extreme-vermorken-2008 src-nccn-hnscc-2025     extreme (vermorken nejm 2008): cetuximab + platinum + 5-fu vs platinum + 5-fu alone in 1l r/m scchn. median os 10.1 vs 7.4 mo (hr 0.80); orr 36% vs 20%. standard 1l for r/m scchn before keynote-048 (2019). now positioned as preferred 1l for: (1) pd-l1 cps <1 (where pembro-chemo benefit is attenuated — keynote-048 cps<1 subgroup hr for os crossed 1.0); (2) io-contraindicated patients (autoimmune disease, prior sot, severe interstitial lung disease). also serves as io-fallback after io failure or rapid progression. cisplatin preferred over carboplatin when feasible. 5-fu civi is resource-intensive (picc line, ambulatory pump); modified tpf and cisplatin + cetuximab + paclitaxel are alternatives in some centers. extreme (cetuximab + cisplatin/carboplatin + 5-fu; hnscc r/m, 1l)  sources: src-esmo-hnscc-2020, src-extreme-vermorken-2008, src-nccn-hnscc-2025 | reviewed 2026-04-30 | pending_clinical_signoff therapieschema

entries.title: Februar-Neutropenie empirische antibakterielle Therapie (Hochrisiko-MASCC < 21 ODER ANC < 100)
entries.subtitle: sources: SRC-ESMO-AML-2020, SRC-NCCN-AML-2025 | reviewed 2026-04-27 | pending_clinical_signoff
entries.search_text: reg-fn-empirical-antibacterial febrile neutropenia empirical antibacterial therapy (high-risk mascc <21 or anc <100) regimen regimen  src-esmo-aml-2020 src-nccn-aml-2025     idsa 2010 + asco 2018 + mascc 2017 + nccn prevention and treatment of cancer-related infections 2024 standard. fn = single oral temperature ≥38.3°c or ≥38°c sustained ≥1h, and anc <500 (or expected to fall <500 within 48h). empirical anti-pseudomonal beta-lactam mono-therapy is the backbone: piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5g iv q8h (extended infusion 4h preferred for severe sepsis), or cefepime 2g iv q8h, or meropenem 1g iv q8h (if prior esbl / resistant gn risk). vancomycin not routine — added only for mrsa-risk subsets. time-to- antibiotic <60 min from fn recognition is critical (mortality surrogate). source-control imperative: blood cultures × 2 (peripheral + central line), urine, sputum, stool c. diff if diarrhea, ct chest early if respiratory symptoms. g-csf recommended for high-risk + sepsis/instability (does not replace antibiotics). daily reassessment for de-escalation, antifungal addition, source localization. this regimen entity is the umbrella — actual prescribing requires institutional antibiogram + clinical judgment + per-patient customization. many supporting drug entities missing — flagged. februar-neutropenie empirische antibakterielle therapie (hochrisiko-mascc < 21 oder anc < 100)  sources: src-esmo-aml-2020, src-nccn-aml-2025 | reviewed 2026-04-27 | pending_clinical_signoff therapieschema

entries.search_text: reg-flot flot regimen regimen  src-esmo-gastric-2024 src-flot4-al-batran-2019 src-nccn-gastric-2025     flot (docetaxel 50 + oxaliplatin 85 + leucovorin 200 + 5-fu 2600 civ/24h q14d) per flot4-aio trial (al-batran 2019, lancet) — global standard perioperative regimen for resectable gastric / gej adenocarcinoma ct2-n+ / locally advanced. used 4 cycles pre-op + 4 cycles post-op (8 total) in periop sequence; pairs with d2 gastrectomy. median os 50 vs 35 mo (hr 0.77; 95% ci 0.63-0.94) vs ecf/ecx. nccn/esmo category 1. toxicity profile is significantly heavier than folfox — taxane component adds neutropenia, alopecia, fluid retention, and ~20-25% febrile-neutropenia risk requiring g-csf primary prophylaxis. flot4 excluded ecog ≥2 patients; clinical fitness assessment is mandatory before initiation. for patients unfit for taxane-containing periop chemotherapy, alternative perioperative regimens (e.g., folfox-based) may be considered after mdt discussion — out of c1 scope. renaissance/aio-flot5 trial (al-batran 2024) examined adding immune checkpoint inhibition to perioperative flot in oligometastatic gastric; not yet a standard-of-care indication and not covered here. flot  sources: src-esmo-gastric-2024, src-flot4-al-batran-2019, src-nccn-gastric-2025 | reviewed 2026-05-07 | pending_clinical_signoff therapieschema

entries.search_text: reg-fruquintinib-crc-3l fruquintinib monotherapy (fresco-2) — 3l+ refractory metastatic crc regimen regimen  src-esmo-crc-2024 src-fresco-2-dasari-2023 src-nccn-colon-2025     fresco-2 phase 3 (dasari lancet 2023): fruquintinib 5 mg po daily 21d on / 7d off vs placebo, refractory metastatic crc after fluoropyrimidine + oxaliplatin + irinotecan ± anti-vegf ± anti-egfr ± tas-102 ± regorafenib (n=691; 461 fruq vs 230 placebo). met primary endpoint mos 7.4 vs 4.8 mo (hr 0.66, p<0.001), mpfs 3.7 vs 1.8 mo (hr 0.32). prior fresco (li jama 2018, chinese cohort only) showed comparable benefit and supported fda bridging. fda approval nov 2023; ema jun 2024. fruquintinib is a highly selective vegfr1/2/3 tki (lower off-target activity than regorafenib / cabozantinib → more favorable hfs / fatigue profile in cross-trial). class toxicity: hypertension (~36%, grade ≥3 14%), proteinuria, hfs, asthenia, hypothyroidism. stub pending clinical co-lead sign-off. nccn-colon-2025 includes fruquintinib as preferred category 1 option in 3l+ refractory mcrc. fruquintinib monotherapie (fresco-2) — 3l+ refraktäre metastasierende crc  sources: src-esmo-crc-2024, src-fresco-2-dasari-2023, src-nccn-colon-2025 | reviewed 2026-04-29 | pending_clinical_signoff therapieschema

entries.search_text: reg-infigratinib-cholangio-2l infigratinib monotherapy (cbgj398x2204) — 2l+ fgfr2-fusion cholangiocarcinoma (historical) regimen regimen  src-esmo-btc-2023 src-nccn-hepatobiliary     cbgj398x2204 (javle jco 2018, javle lancet gastroenterol hepatol 2021): infigratinib 125 mg po daily 21d on / 7d off, advanced / metastatic cholangiocarcinoma with fgfr2 fusion / rearrangement post-≥1l gemcitabine-based therapy (n=108). orr 23.1% (25/108), dcr 84.3%, mdor 5.0 mo, mpfs 7.3 mo, mos 12.2 mo. fda accelerated approval may 2021. withdrawn voluntarily aug-sep 2022 (helsinn divested oncology portfolio; qed therapeutics ceased commercial operations) — not a safety withdrawal. subsequent fgfr-tkis (pemigatinib fight-202, futibatinib foenix-cca2) replaced infigratinib in nccn / esmo guidance. class toxicity profile identical to other reversible fgfr1-3 tkis: hyperphosphatemia (~76%), retinal detachment, alopecia, nail toxicity. stub pending clinical co-lead sign-off; flagged historical — render layer must not surface as an active recommendation. bibliographic record src-cbgj398x2204 is available as historical evidence; source-to-claim mapping requires dual clinical sign-off. infigratinib-monotherapie (cbgj398x2204) — 2l+ fgfr2-fusionscholangiokarzinom (historisches)  sources: src-esmo-btc-2023, src-nccn-hepatobiliary | reviewed 2026-04-29 | pending_clinical_signoff therapieschema

entries.search_text: reg-irr-rescue-protocol infusion reaction rescue protocol (mab / chemotherapy irr grade ≥2) regimen regimen  src-esmo-dlbcl-2024 src-nccn-bcell-2025     ctcae v5.0 irr grading + nccn/esmo/mascc anaphylaxis management framework. highest-risk agents for irr: rituximab cycle 1 (~75% any-grade, ~10% g3+), obinutuzumab cycle 1 day 1 (~65%), daratumumab cycle 1 (~50% iv; ~13% sc), amivantamab cycle 1 day 1 (~65% iv; ~13% sc), cetuximab cycle 1 (~3% g3+; se us ~20% with alpha-gal ige), paclitaxel (~10% any-grade; cremophor vehicle hypersensitivity), carboplatin/oxaliplatin (cumulative; cycles 6+ — true ige-mediated, desensitization protocol indicated), l-asparaginase (anaphylaxis ~5-10% with native e. coli formulation; less with peg-asparaginase / erwinia), bleomycin (rare; idiosyncratic). premedication standard: acetaminophen 650-1000 mg po + diphenhydramine 25-50 mg po/iv + ranitidine 50 mg iv (or famotidine 20 mg iv) ≥30 min before infusion; add iv steroid for high-risk agents (rituximab cycle 1, obinutuzumab cycle 1, daratumumab cycle 1, amivantamab cycle 1, taxanes). slow first-cycle infusion rate is universally protective. desensitization (incremental dose escalation over 3-4h with 12-step protocol) allows continuation of life-saving therapy in true ige-mediated reactions — requires allergy/immunology + icu-capable setting. infusionsreaktionsrettungsprotokoll (mab / chemotherapie irr grad ≥2)  sources: src-esmo-dlbcl-2024, src-nccn-bcell-2025 | reviewed 2026-04-27 | pending_clinical_signoff therapieschema

entries.title: Isatuximab + Carfilzomib + Dexamethasone (Isa-Kd), 28-day cycles
entries.subtitle: sources: SRC-EHA-EMN-MM-2025, SRC-IKEMA-MOREAU-2021, SRC-NCCN-MM-2025 | reviewed 2026-05-07 | pending_clinical_signoff
entries.search_text: reg-isa-kd-mm-3l isatuximab + carfilzomib + dexamethasone (isa-kd), 28-day cycles regimen regimen  src-eha-emn-mm-2025 src-ikema-moreau-2021 src-nccn-mm-2025     ikema trial (moreau 2021, nejm): in r/r mm after 1-3 prior lines including a pi and an imid, isa-kd (n=179) vs kd (n=123). primary endpoint: pfs hr 0.531 (95% ci 0.318-0.889; p=0.0014); 18-month pfs ~68% vs 50%. orr 86.6% vs 82.9%; mrd negativity (10^-5) 29.6% vs 13.0%. isatuximab dosing in cycle 1 is weekly (days 1, 8, 15, 22) then biweekly from cycle 2 (days 1, 15). carfilzomib ramp-up: 20 mg/m^2 days 1-2 cycle 1, then 56 mg/m^2. dexamethasone 20 mg on 8 days per cycle (premedication overlap with isatuximab irr prophylaxis on infusion days). near-equivalent alternative to dkd (candor) — choose based on drug access; no head-to-head data. anti-cd38 (isatuximab) interferes with red-cell crossmatch — dat/coombs baseline mandatory before cycle 1. isatuximab + carfilzomib + dexamethasone (isa-kd), 28-day cycles  sources: src-eha-emn-mm-2025, src-ikema-moreau-2021, src-nccn-mm-2025 | reviewed 2026-05-07 | pending_clinical_signoff therapieschema

entries.subtitle: sources: SRC-CLARIDHY-ABOU-ALFA-2020, SRC-ESMO-BTC-2023, SRC-NCCN-HEPATOBILIARY | reviewed 2026-05-07 | pending_clinical_signoff
entries.search_text: reg-ivosidenib-cholangio ivosidenib monotherapy (claridhy) — 2l+ idh1-mutated cholangiocarcinoma regimen regimen  src-claridhy-abou-alfa-2020 src-esmo-btc-2023 src-nccn-hepatobiliary     claridhy phase 3 (abou-alfa et al. lancet oncol 2020): ivosidenib 500 mg po daily continuous vs placebo in advanced/metastatic idh1-mutant cholangiocarcinoma post ≥1l systemic therapy (typically gemcitabine/cisplatin ± durvalumab in modern practice). n=185 randomized 2:1 (ivo n=124, pbo n=61). mpfs 2.7 vs 1.4 mo, hr 0.37 (95% ci 0.25–0.54), p<0.0001. disease control rate 53% vs 28%. orr 2% (no cr; 2 pr by independent review). mos hr 0.79 itt (ns, with 70.5% placebo-arm crossover); rpsft-adjusted mos hr 0.49 — os benefit recognized in label. fda-approved august 2021; ema approved 2023. toxicity well tolerated overall (g≥3 ae 30% ivo vs 22% pbo); notable aes: ascites (g≥3 7% ivo vs 5% pbo, attributable to disease progression in part), fatigue, nausea, qtc prolongation (any grade ~9%, g≥3 ~1%). differentiation syndrome — boxed warning class effect — not observed in claridhy cholangio cohort but possible per labelling and aml experience; clinicians should remain aware. stub pending clinical co-lead sign-off; src-claridhy-abou-alfa-2020 ingested as primary citation (w0-cholangio pr #456). ivosidenib-monotherapie (claridhy) — 2l+ idh1-mutiertes cholangiokarzinom  sources: src-claridhy-abou-alfa-2020, src-esmo-btc-2023, src-nccn-hepatobiliary | reviewed 2026-05-07 | pending_clinical_signoff therapieschema

entries.search_text: reg-lanreotide-autogel-gi-net lanreotide autogel 120 mg sc q4w (well-differentiated gep-net g1/g2; clarinet) regimen regimen  src-clarinet-caplin-2014 src-nccn-net-2025     clarinet (caplin nejm 2014): lanreotide 120 mg q4w vs placebo in well-differentiated g1/g2 non-functioning gep-net (n=204). mpfs not reached vs 18.0 mo (hr 0.47, p<0.001). also shown in promid (rinke jco 2009) with octreotide lar 30 mg q4w for midgut net: mpfs 14.3 vs 6.0 mo (hr 0.34). both trials establish ssa as antiproliferative standard (not just symptom control). clarinet ole (96-week extension) confirmed durable benefit in stable/non-progressive disease. octreotide lar 30 mg q4w is a valid alternative to lanreotide (no head-to-head; both nccn category 1 for gi-net). lanreotide used here as it has the broader clarinet gep-net data set. stub pending §6.1 signoff. lanreotide autogel 120 mg sc q4w (well-differentiated gep-net g1/g2; clarinet)  sources: src-clarinet-caplin-2014, src-nccn-net-2025 | reviewed 2026-05-03 | pending_clinical_signoff therapieschema

entries.title: Lenalidomide + Dexamethasone continuous (Rd, MAIA control arm — MM 1L transplant-ineligible)
entries.subtitle: sources: SRC-MAIA-FACON-2019, SRC-NCCN-MM-2025 | reviewed 2026-05-09 | pending_clinical_signoff
entries.search_text: reg-rd-continuous lenalidomide + dexamethasone continuous (rd, maia control arm — mm 1l transplant-ineligible) regimen regimen  src-maia-facon-2019 src-nccn-mm-2025     rd continuous (lenalidomide + low-dose dexamethasone until progression) was the maia control arm (facon nejm 2019, pmid 30926586) and represents the standard-access first-line regimen for transplant-ineligible ndmm. maia control arm outcomes: orr 75.8%, pfs hr (d-rd vs rd) 0.56 (95% ci 0.43–0.73), 30-month pfs ~53.3% for d-rd vs ~37.8% for rd. rd continuous showed superiority over mpt and melphalan-prednisone in the first trial (benboubker nejm 2014, pmid 25184863): pfs 26 months vs 21.9 months for mpt. dose of dexamethasone: low-dose (40 mg weekly = "ld schedule") is preferred over high-dose (480 mg/cycle); ecog e4a03 showed equivalent efficacy and better tolerability with low-dose dex in ndmm (rajkumar lancet oncol 2010). renal adjustment is critical: lenalidomide is ~80% renally cleared. crcl 30-60 → 10 mg daily; crcl <30 → 5 mg daily or 10 mg qod. myeloma renal impairment often improves with therapy — recheck crcl monthly and escalate dose when gfr recovers. second primary malignancy (spm) risk: calgb 100104 and ifm 2005-02 documented elevated spm (mds/aml) with lenalidomide maintenance post-asct; risk applies to continuous rd as well at smaller magnitude. must be included in informed consent discussion. lenalidomide + dexamethasone continuous (rd, maia control arm — mm 1l transplant-ineligible)  sources: src-maia-facon-2019, src-nccn-mm-2025 | reviewed 2026-05-09 | pending_clinical_signoff therapieschema

entries.search_text: regimen-lisocel-dlbcl-2l lisocabtagene maraleucel (liso-cel) car-t 2l for primary-refractory or early-relapse lbcl (transform) regimen regimen  src-esmo-dlbcl-2024 src-nccn-bcell-2025     cd19 car-t (4-1bb costimulation) with defined 1:1 cd4:cd8 cell composition for primary-refractory lbcl or relapse <12 months from completion of first-line therapy. transform phase 3 rct (kamdar et al., lancet 2022; long-term update abramson et al., blood 2023): liso-cel superior to standard-of-care salvage chemo + autosct in transplant-intended 2l primary-refractory / early-relapse lbcl — median efs 10.1 vs 2.3 mo (hr ~0.36), cr ~74% vs ~43%, pfs substantially extended; os trend favourable but crossover-confounded. boxed warnings: crs, icans, secondary t-cell malignancy (fda 2024 class label). rems / fact-jacie-accredited centre mandatory. eligibility narrower than 3l: primary-refractory or early-relapse + transplant-intent. distinct from regimen-lisocel-dlbcl-3l (transcend, ≥3l any-comer). trial source src-transform-kamdar-2022 absent from kb at chunk authoring time — citing nccn-bcell-2025 + esmo-dlbcl-2024 pending source-stub creation. lisocabtagene maraleucel (liso-cel) car-t 2l für primär-refraktäre oder früh-rezidivierende lbcl (transform)  sources: src-esmo-dlbcl-2024, src-nccn-bcell-2025 | reviewed 2026-05-01 | pending_clinical_signoff therapieschema

entries.search_text: reg-nalirifox nalirifox regimen regimen  src-esmo-pancreatic-2024 src-napoli-3-wainberg-2024 src-nccn-pancreatic-2025     napoli-3 (wainberg, lancet 2023; n=770, phase 3 rct; nct04083235): nalirifox vs gem-nab-pac as 1l therapy in metastatic pdac, ecog 0-1. mos 11.1 vs 9.2 mo (hr 0.83, 95% ci 0.70-0.99, p=0.04); mpfs 7.4 vs 5.6 mo (hr 0.69, 95% ci 0.58-0.83, p<0.0001); orr 41.8% vs 36.2%. grade ≥3 teaes comparable: diarrhea (20% vs 4.5%), nausea (12% vs 3%), hypokalemia (15% vs 4%), neutropenia (14% vs 25%), febrile neutropenia (3% vs 1%), peripheral neuropathy (3% vs 2%), thrombocytopenia (2% vs 9%). nccn category 1 (preferred) 1l option for mpdac alongside folfirinox and gem-nab-pac. eligibility: ps 0-1, bilirubin <1.5-2× uln, no severe cardiac comorbidity. nalirifox vs folfirinox: no head-to-head trial; cross-trial os appears comparable; nalirifox may have somewhat better tolerability profile (lower neutropenia, less alopecia) but more diarrhea and nausea. choice between folfirinox and nalirifox in ukraine is dominated by onivyde access (not registered) — folfirinox remains the accessible category 1 option. between_visit_watchpoints authoring deferred to patient_mode phase 3 backlog. nalirifox  sources: src-esmo-pancreatic-2024, src-napoli-3-wainberg-2024, src-nccn-pancreatic-2025 | reviewed 2026-05-08 | pending_clinical_signoff therapieschema

entries.search_text: reg-nivo-ipi-chemo-nsclc-1l nivolumab + ipilimumab + 2-cycle platinum-doublet chemotherapy (checkmate-9la) regimen regimen  src-checkmate-9la-paz-ares-2021     checkmate-9la (nct03215706) regimen: nivolumab 360 mg q3w + ipilimumab 1 mg/kg q6w (dual io backbone, same as checkmate-227 part 1) combined with 2 cycles of histology-directed platinum-doublet chemotherapy. rationale for 2 chemo cycles: rapid early disease control while io ramps up; minimizes cumulative chemo toxicity. histology-specific chemo component (both used in cycles 1–2 only): - squamous: carboplatin auc 6 + paclitaxel 200 mg/m² day 1 (or nab-paclitaxel 100 mg/m² days 1/8/15 per amendment) - non-squamous: carboplatin auc 5 + pemetrexed 500 mg/m² (add folate/b12 supplementation) after 2 chemo cycles, continue nivolumab 360 mg q3w + ipilimumab 1 mg/kg q6w alone until progression, unacceptable toxicity, or 2 years of ipilimumab cumulative exposure. key distinction from checkmate-227 (nivo+ipi alone): addition of 2-cycle chemo provides faster initial tumor control, higher early orr (38% vs ~32%), and broader benefit independent of pd-l1 tps (tps <1% subgroup hr 0.62 for os in checkmate-9la). drug-ipilimumab confirmed present in kb (knowledge_base/hosted/content/drugs/ipilimumab.yaml, id: drug-ipilimumab). nivolumab + ipilimumab+ 2-zyklus-platin-doppelchemotherapie (checkmate-9la)  quellen: src-checkmate-9la-paz-ares-2021--- überprüft 2026-05-07-- ausstehende_klinische_signoff therapieschema

entries.search_text: reg-paclitaxel-kaposi paclitaxel monotherapy (kaposi sarcoma, post-anthracycline) regimen regimen       new regimen entity reusing the existing drug-paclitaxel drug entity. drug-paclitaxel already documents "kaposi sarcoma (aids-related, 2l)" as an fda-approved indication (regulatory_status.fda.indications_brief -- pre-existing fact, transcribed not invented, verified by direct read of drugs/paclitaxel.yaml during independent review) but its typical_dosing field does not carry a kaposi-specific mg/m²/schedule figure, and no kb-verifiable primary source for that figure was available at authoring time. per charter §8.3 ("must never invent a dose ..."), the `dose`/`schedule` component fields are deliberately left as an explicit flagged gap rather than a fabricated number -- this is an intentional, disclosed omission, not an authoring oversight. the mandatory cremophor-el hypersensitivity premedication is transcribed from the existing drug-paclitaxel entity because that fact is dose-independent and already verified in the kb. independent review correction (2026-07-11): an earlier draft cited src-nccn-skin-2025 for the dose-adjustment items and the file's top-level sources. that source documents only basal-cell/squamous- cell skin cancer (confirmed by direct inspection of its own kb record) and does not mention kaposi sarcoma, so citing it here would misrepresent evidentiary support; it was removed (`sources: []`, empty `source_refs`). this regimen has no verified source for either its (deliberately omitted) dose or its toxicity-management content beyond the reused drug-paclitaxel entity itself -- a real, fully-disclosed evidentiary gap. stub pending two-clinical-co-lead signoff (charter §6.1 -- dev-mode-exempted; safe to merge as draft content, not as published/verified clinical advice; this regimen additionally requires a dosing fill-in before it could ever be used clinically). paclitaxel-monotherapie (kaposi-sarkom, post-anthracyclin)  überprüft 2026-07-11-- anhängig_klinisch_signoff therapieschema

entries.search_text: reg-pld-kaposi pegylated liposomal doxorubicin monotherapy (kaposi sarcoma) regimen regimen       new regimen entity reusing the existing drug-pegylated-liposomal- doxorubicin drug entity. the 20 mg/m² iv q2-3wk kaposi sarcoma dose and toxicity-management triggers (hold thresholds for ppe, stomatitis, anc/platelet nadir, lvef decline) are transcribed directly from that already-existing drug entity's `typical_dosing`/`notes` fields (which independently document "kaposi sarcoma: 20 mg/m² iv every 2-3 weeks" and the hold criteria -- verified by direct read of drugs/pegylated_liposomal_doxorubicin.yaml during independent review) -- not a newly invented figure. pegylated liposomal doxorubicin is fda-approved for aids-related kaposi sarcoma (see drug-pegylated-liposomal-doxorubicin.regulatory_status.fda. indications_brief). independent review correction (2026-07-11): an earlier draft cited src-nccn-skin-2025 throughout this file (top-level sources, every dose-adjustment, every watchpoint) as the evidentiary support for the dosing/toxicity-management content above. direct inspection of that source's own kb record (sources/src_nccn_skin_2025.yaml) shows its title is "nccn clinical practice guidelines in oncology: basal cell skin cancer" and its notes explicitly scope it to basal-cell and squamous-cell skin cancer -- kaposi sarcoma is not mentioned. citing it as if it substantiated this regimen's kaposi-specific dosing/toxicity content would misrepresent evidentiary support, so all such citations were removed (`sources: []`, empty `source_refs` / watchpoint `sources`). the underlying dosing facts remain non-fabricated (see above -- transcribed from the existing drug entity), but no independent kaposi-sarcoma-specific trial or guideline source is cited in this file. this is a real, disclosed evidentiary gap flagged for future ingestion of a dedicated kaposi-sarcoma-chemotherapy primary source (e.g. a pld-vs-abv randomized comparison), which was not named in the authoring narrative and so was not fabricated as a new source stub. stub pending two-clinical-co-lead signoff (charter §6.1 -- dev-mode- exempted; safe to merge as draft content, not as published/verified clinical advice). pegylated liposomal doxorubicin monotherapy (kaposi sarcoma)  überprüft 2026-07-11-- entries.search_text: reg-pembrolizumab-cervical-1l pembrolizumab + carboplatin + paclitaxel ± bevacizumab (persistent/recurrent/metastatic cervical 1l pd-l1 cps ≥1, keynote-826) regimen regimen  src-esmo-cervical-2024 src-keynote-826-colombo-2021 src-nccn-cervical-2025     keynote-826 (colombo nejm 2021, n=617) established pembrolizumab + platinum-doublet (carboplatin or cisplatin + paclitaxel) ± bevacizumab as 1l standard for persistent / recurrent / metastatic cervical cancer with pd-l1 cps ≥1 (which is ~88% of cervical cancers). pfs hr 0.65 (95% ci 0.53–0.79), os hr 0.67 (95% ci 0.54–0.84) in cps ≥1 population; benefit consistent across all pre-specified subgroups including bevacizumab-add stratum. fda approval oct 2021 (cps ≥1); ema approval 2022. bevacizumab add-on per investigator discretion in keynote-826 — recommended where no contraindication (no high fistula risk from prior pelvic rt, no controlled hypertension, no recent surgery, no thromboembolic history). pd-l1 cps testing by 22c3 ihc is the companion biomarker. standard pd-1 irae spectrum + bevacizumab class aes (htn, proteinuria, fistula risk); cervical- specific fistula concern given prior pelvic rt in many patients. pembrolizumab + carboplatin + paclitaxel ± bevacizumab (persistent/recurrent/metastastisch zervikale 1l pd-l1 cps ≥1, keynote-826)  sources: src-esmo-cervical-2024, src-keynote-826-colombo-2021, src-nccn-cervical-2025 | reviewed 2026-04-29 | pending_clinical_signoff therapieschema

entries.title: Pembrolizumab + cisplatin-based chemo (NSCLC neoadjuvant; KEYNOTE-671)
entries.subtitle: sources: SRC-ESMO-NSCLC-EARLY-2024, SRC-KEYNOTE-671-WAKELEE-2023, SRC-NCCN-NSCLC-2025 | reviewed 2026-05-09 | pending_clinical_signoff
entries.search_text: reg-pembro-chemo-neoadj-nsclc pembrolizumab + cisplatin-based chemo (nsclc neoadjuvant; keynote-671) regimen regimen  src-esmo-nsclc-early-2024 src-keynote-671-wakelee-2023 src-nccn-nsclc-2025     keynote-671 (wakelee nejm 2023, spicer nejm 2024 os update): neoadjuvant pembrolizumab 200 mg q3w + cisplatin-based doublet × 4 cycles followed by surgery and adjuvant pembrolizumab × 13 cycles, in resectable stage ii/iiia/iiib (t3-t4n2) nsclc. 24-mo efs 62.4% vs 40.6% (hr 0.58, p<0.001); pcr 18.1% vs 4.0%; mpr 30.2% vs 11.0%; os update mos not reached vs 52.4 mo (hr 0.72, p=0.005). fda approval oct 2023; nccn v3.2025 category 1. trial protocol used cisplatin-based doublet specifically: * non-squamous: cisplatin 75 mg/m² + pemetrexed 500 mg/m² q3w * squamous: cisplatin 75 mg/m² + gemcitabine 1000 mg/m² days 1+8 q3w carboplatin (auc 5) substitution for cisplatin is nccn-allowed as a real-world tolerability variant in patients with renal impairment, ototoxicity, neuropathy, or other cisplatin-contraindications, but is not the trial protocol — note this in the plan rationale when carbo is substituted. pembrolizumab is administered concurrently with chemo cycles 1-4 (neoadjuvant), then continues post-resection as adjuvant monotherapy × 13 cycles (reg-pembro-adjuvant-nsclc) for total ~17 cycles pembrolizumab over the perioperative course. excludes patients with egfr-activating mutations or alk fusion — driver-positive resectable nsclc has superior adjuvant tki options (osimertinib per adaura, alectinib per alina) and io efficacy is reduced in driver-positive disease (fda label requires egfr/alk testing before perioperative pembro initiation). pembrolizumab + cisplatin-based chemo (nsclc neoadjuvant; keynote-671)  sources: src-esmo-nsclc-early-2024, src-keynote-671-wakelee-2023, src-nccn-nsclc-2025 | reviewed 2026-05-09 | pending_clinical_signoff therapieschema

entries.search_text: reg-pembro-gem-cis-cholangio pembrolizumab + gemcitabine + cisplatin (keynote-966) — 1l advanced biliary tract cancer regimen regimen  src-esmo-btc-2023 src-keynote-966-kelley-2023 src-nccn-hepatobiliary     keynote-966 (kelley rk et al., lancet 2023;401(10391):1853-1865; nct04003636): pembrolizumab 200 mg q3w + gemcitabine 1000 mg/m² + cisplatin 25 mg/m² (d1, d8 q3w; cisplatin capped at 8 cycles, gem continued indefinitely with pembro), vs placebo + gem-cis in 1l advanced btc (n=1069). primary endpoint os: mos 12.7 vs 10.9 mo (hr 0.83, 95% ci 0.72-0.95, p=0.0034); mpfs 6.5 vs 5.6 mo (hr 0.86, ns); orr 29% vs 29% (no improvement). benefit consistent across pd-l1 cps subgroups; magnitude smaller than topaz-1 but corroborates anti-pd-(l)1 + chemo as new 1l standard. fda-approved oct 2023. nccn category 1 alternative preferred regimen alongside topaz-1. note: keynote-966 differs from topaz-1 in that gemcitabine continues past 8 cycles as maintenance with pembrolizumab (cisplatin capped at cycle 8); topaz-1 stops both gem and cis at cycle 8 with durvalumab monotherapy maintenance. stub pending clinical co-lead sign-off per charter §6.1 dev-mode exemption. pembrolizumab + gemcitabine + cisplatin (keynote-966) — 1l advanced biliary tract cancer  sources: src-esmo-btc-2023, src-keynote-966-kelley-2023, src-nccn-hepatobiliary | reviewed 2026-05-08 | pending_clinical_signoff therapieschema

entries.search_text: reg-pembro-adjuvant-nsclc pembrolizumab adjuvant (resected nsclc; keynote-671) regimen regimen  src-esmo-nsclc-early-2024 src-keynote-671-wakelee-2023 src-nccn-nsclc-2025     keynote-671 adjuvant phase (wakelee nejm 2023): pembrolizumab 200 mg q3w × 13 cycles (~9 months) starting within 4-12 weeks of complete surgical resection, following 4 cycles of neoadjuvant pembrolizumab + cisplatin-based doublet (reg-pembro-chemo-neoadj-nsclc). total perioperative pembrolizumab exposure: 17 cycles / ~1 year. efs hr 0.58 and os hr 0.72 reflect the contribution of the full perioperative package; adjuvant phase contribution is not independently dissectable from the trial design. distinct from reg-pembro-adjuvant-melanoma (18 cycles, keynote-054 protocol) — separate regimen entity to capture the keynote-671-specific cycle count and nsclc-specific monitoring (post-resection pneumonitis baseline elevated; lower irae-discontinuation threshold). excludes patients with egfr-activating mutations or alk fusion (fda label) — driver-positive resectable nsclc has superior adjuvant tki options (osimertinib per adaura, alectinib per alina). pembrolizumab adjuvant (befallener nsclc; keynote-671)  sources: src-esmo-nsclc-early-2024, src-keynote-671-wakelee-2023, src-nccn-nsclc-2025 | reviewed 2026-05-09 | pending_clinical_signoff therapieschema

entries.search_text: reg-pembro-adjuvant-melanoma pembrolizumab adjuvant (resected stage iii/iv melanoma; keynote-054) regimen regimen  src-esmo-melanoma-2024 src-keynote-054-eggermont-2018 src-nccn-melanoma-2025     keynote-054 / eortc-1325 (eggermont nejm 2018, lancet oncol 2021 5-yr update): adjuvant pembrolizumab 200 mg q3w × 1 yr vs placebo in resected stage iii melanoma (n=1019). 12-mo rfs 75.4% vs 61.0% (hr 0.57); 5-yr rfs 55.4% vs 38.3% (hr 0.61); benefit consistent across pd-l1+ and pd-l1- subgroups. established adjuvant pembrolizumab for resected stage iii; basis for fda approval feb 2019 + later expansion to stage iib/iic (keynote-716). start within 12 weeks of surgery; complete 18 cycles unless recurrence / intolerance. adjuvant nivolumab (checkmate-238) is interchangeable alternative. pembrolizumab adjuvant (befallenes melanom im stadium iii/iv; keynote-054)  sources: src-esmo-melanoma-2024, src-keynote-054-eggermont-2018, src-nccn-melanoma-2025 | reviewed 2026-04-30 | pending_clinical_signoff therapieschema
