entries.search_text: reg-pembro-mono-melanoma pembrolizumab monotherapy (advanced/metastatic melanoma, 1l; keynote-006) regimen regimen  src-esmo-melanoma-2024 src-keynote-006-robert-2015 src-nccn-melanoma-2025     keynote-006 (robert nejm 2015 + lancet oncol 2023 7-yr update): pembrolizumab q2w or q3w vs ipilimumab in 1l unresectable / metastatic melanoma (n=834). 6-mo pfs 47% vs 26% (hr 0.58); 12-mo os 74% vs 58% (hr 0.69). 7-yr os ~37% pembro vs ~25% ipi. pd-l1-agnostic; basis for fda approval dec 2015. single-agent anti-pd-1 is preferred when ipi+nivo combination toxicity is unacceptable (irae-frail, autoimmune comorbidity, advanced age, ecog 2). lower g3-4 irae rate (~17%) vs ipi+nivo (~55%). long-tail responders typical of io. pembrolizumab monotherapie (fortgeschrittenes/metastatisches melanom, 1l; keynote-006)  sources: src-esmo-melanoma-2024, src-keynote-006-robert-2015, src-nccn-melanoma-2025 | reviewed 2026-04-30 | pending_clinical_signoff therapieschema

entries.title: Sirolimus-Umwandlung (iatrogenes/transplantiertes Kaposi-Sarkom)
entries.subtitle: überprüft 2026-07-11-- anhängig_klinisch_signoff
entries.search_text: reg-sirolimus-kaposi-conversion sirolimus conversion (iatrogenic/transplant-associated kaposi sarcoma) regimen regimen       new regimen entity -- reuses the existing drug-sirolimus drug entity (already in the kb for the lam indication) but is authored separately from reg-sirolimus-lam because the clinical context (transplant immunosuppression-conversion vs. lam antiproliferative monotherapy), monitoring priorities (graft function vs. pulmonary function), and evidence base differ. dosing is deliberately described qualitatively ("per transplant-team protocol") rather than with a single asserted mg/target-trough number: no kb-verifiable primary source for a kaposi-conversion-specific sirolimus target trough was available at authoring time (charter §8.3 -- do not invent a numeric threshold not already stated in a verified source). conversion from calcineurin- inhibitor-based to mtor-inhibitor-based immunosuppression for post-transplant kaposi sarcoma is well described in the transplant literature (documented tumor regression in a meaningful fraction of patients) but must always be transplant-team-directed -- graft rejection is a real risk. independent review correction (2026-07-11): an earlier draft cited src-nih-aids-2024 as the source for this regimen's dose-adjustment and between-visit-watchpoint items. that source is the nih hhs antiretroviral / opportunistic-infection guideline set (confirmed from its own kb record) and does not address transplant immunosuppression management, mtor-inhibitor conversion, or sirolimus dosing/toxicity -- citing it here would misrepresent evidentiary support, so all such citations were removed (`sources: []`, empty `source_refs` / watchpoint `sources`). the underlying drug-class toxicity facts (stomatitis, pneumonitis, dyslipidemia, impaired wound healing) are drawn from the already-verified drug-sirolimus entity itself, not fabricated. this is a real, disclosed evidentiary gap -- no kaposi-specific transplant-conversion source is cited anywhere in this file. stub pending two-clinical-co-lead signoff (charter §6.1 -- dev-mode- exempted; safe to merge as draft content, not as published/verified clinical advice). sirolimus-umwandlung (iatrogenes/transplantiertes kaposi-sarkom)  überprüft 2026-07-11-- anhängig_klinisch_signoff therapieschema

entries.search_text: reg-talazoparib-mono-breast talazoparib monotherapy (gbrca-mutant her2- locally advanced or metastatic breast) regimen regimen  src-embraca-litton-2018 src-esmo-breast-metastatic-2024 src-nccn-breast-2025     embraca (nct01945775): phase iii, gbrca1/2-mutant her2- locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer (≤3 prior cytotoxic regimens for advanced disease). talazoparib 1 mg po daily vs physician's- choice single-agent chemo (capecitabine / eribulin / gemcitabine / vinorelbine). median pfs 8.6 vs 5.6 mo (hr 0.54); orr 62.6% vs 27.2%. os not significantly different at final analysis (hr 0.85, p=0.17). fda approval oct 2018. greater parp-trapping potency than olaparib — anemia is dose-limiting ae (~53% any grade, ~39% g≥3); transfusion support frequently required. germline brca1/2 testing (peripheral blood) required pre-start. monotherapy alternative to olaparib olympiad; head-to-head not done. talazoparib monotherapie (gbrca-mutante her2- lokal fortgeschrittene oder metastasierende brust)  sources: src-embraca-litton-2018, src-esmo-breast-metastatic-2024, src-nccn-breast-2025 | pending_clinical_signoff therapieschema

entries.title: Tarlatamab — 2L+ extensive SCLC (DeLLphi-301; DLL3 × CD3 BiTE)
entries.subtitle: sources: SRC-DELLPHI-301-AHN-2023, SRC-ESMO-SCLC-2021, SRC-NCCN-SCLC-2025 | reviewed 2026-05-08 | pending_clinical_signoff
entries.search_text: reg-tarlatamab tarlatamab — 2l+ extensive-stage sclc (dellphi-301; dll3 × cd3 bite) regimen regimen  src-dellphi-301-ahn-2023 src-esmo-sclc-2021 src-nccn-sclc-2025     dellphi-301 (ahn et al., nejm 2023; nct05060016): open-label multicenter phase 2 trial of tarlatamab (dll3 × cd3 bispecific t-cell engager) in pretreated extensive-stage sclc progressing on or after platinum-based chemotherapy. 222 patients randomized 1:1 to 10 mg q2w vs 100 mg q2w. 10 mg q2w cohort (n=99) — confirmed orr per independent central review 40% (95% ci 29-52); mdor not reached at 10.6 mo follow-up; mpfs 4.9 mo; mos 14.3 mo (95% ci 10.8-ne). 100 mg cohort showed similar orr with higher crs rate; 10 mg selected as registered dose. crs any-grade ~50% (mostly cycle 1 d1-d2 fever ± mild hypotension); grade ≥3 crs ~1%. icans-like neurotoxicity grade ≥3 ~7%. step-up dosing (1 mg → 10 mg) + inpatient cycle 1 d1 + d8 monitoring (22+ hr) is mandatory per us prescribing information; mitigates crs through immune-effector priming. tocilizumab + corticosteroids first-line for grade ≥2 crs / icans. fda accelerated approval may 2024. nccn-sclc 2025 category 2a for es-sclc 2l+ post-platinum. confirmatory phase 3 dellphi-304 (tarlatamab vs investigator-choice chemotherapy in 2l es-sclc) ongoing. active development: maintenance post-1l chemo-io (dellphi-303); sclc-transformed nsclc; neuroendocrine prostate cancer. pending peer-reviewed pop-pk and label updates may further refine step-up schedule. tarlatamab — 2l+ extensive sclc (dellphi-301; dll3 × cd3 bite)  sources: src-dellphi-301-ahn-2023, src-esmo-sclc-2021, src-nccn-sclc-2025 | reviewed 2026-05-08 | pending_clinical_signoff therapieschema

entries.search_text: reg-zanidatamab zanidatamab — 2l+ her2-amplified biliary tract cancer (herizon-btc-01) regimen regimen  src-esmo-btc-2023 src-herizon-btc-01-harding-2023 src-nccn-hepatobiliary     herizon-btc-01 (harding et al., lancet oncol 2023; nct04466891): single-arm phase 2b trial of zanidatamab 20 mg/kg iv q2w in her2- amplified (ihc 3+ or ihc 2+/ish+) unresectable / locally advanced / metastatic biliary tract cancer progressed on prior gemcitabine- based therapy; primary efficacy cohort 1 (her2 ihc 3+ or ihc 2+/ish+) n=87 — confirmed orr per independent central review 41.3% (95% ci 30.4-52.8); dcr 68.8%; median dor 14.9 mo. treatment-related grade ≥3 aes in 18%; no treatment-related deaths. most common aes: diarrhea (~40%), infusion-related reactions (~33%), nausea, fatigue. single-arm phase 2b — evidence tier 2 / moderate (no randomised comparator). fda accelerated approval november 2024 for previously treated her2-positive (ihc 3+) btc. nccn category 2a; escat tier iia (fda-approved disease-specific). confirmatory phase 3 (herizon-gea-01 in her2+ gastric/gej) and ongoing btc studies pending. ua access: named-patient / eap only as of 2026-05. zanidatamab — 2l+ her2-verstärkte gallenwegskrebse (herizon-btc-01)  sources: src-esmo-btc-2023, src-herizon-btc-01-harding-2023, src-nccn-hepatobiliary | reviewed 2026-05-08 | pending_clinical_signoff therapieschema

entries.search_text: reg-zanubrutinib-continuous zanubrutinib monotherapy (continuous, alpine-style) regimen regimen  src-esmo-cll-2024 src-nccn-bcell-2025     alpine trial (brown 2023): in r/r cll, zanubrutinib superior to ibrutinib in pfs (hr 0.65) and cardiac safety (afib 5.2% vs 13.3%; cardiac death 0% vs 1.9%). sequoia trial: 1l cll, zanubrutinib vs bendamustine-rituximab — superior pfs. combined: zanubrutinib is preferred btki for both 1l (sequoia) and r/r (alpine) cll where accessible. acalabrutinib (reg-acalabrutinib-continuous, elevate-tn/rr) is the alternative second-generation btki with similar safety profile. zanubrutinib monotherapie (kontinuierlich, alpine-stil)  sources: src-esmo-cll-2024, src-nccn-bcell-2025 | reviewed 2026-04-25 | pending_clinical_signoff therapieschema

entries.title: Zanubrutinib monotherapy continuous for r/r WM (ASPEN schedule) — alternative to ibrutinib

entries.search_text: reg-zanubrutinib-wm-relapsed zanubrutinib monotherapy continuous for r/r wm (aspen schedule) — alternative to ibrutinib regimen regimen  src-esmo-wm-2024 src-nccn-bcell-2025     aspen trial (tam 2020, follow-up 2023): r/r wm (and 1l cohort) — zanubrutinib superior to ibrutinib in safety profile (afib 2.6% vs 15.3%; cardiac death 0% vs 1.6%; major bleeding 4% vs 9%; hypertension 13% vs 25%); comparable vgpr-or-better hematologic response (28% vs 19% in myd88-mut cohort, numerically superior). preferred btki for r/r wm where accessible. cxcr4-whim-mutated subset has reduced depth of response with both btkis — consider proteasome-inhibitor (carfilzomib) alternative for these patients. zanubrutinib monotherapy continuous for r/r wm (aspen schedule) — alternative to ibrutinib  sources: src-esmo-wm-2024, src-nccn-bcell-2025 | reviewed 2026-04-25 | pending_clinical_signoff therapieschema

entries.title: Zenocutuzumab Monotherapie (eNRGy) — NRG1-fusion+ NSCLC (pan-Tumor-Aktivität)
entries.subtitle: sources: SRC-ESMO-NSCLC-METASTATIC-2024, SRC-NCCN-NSCLC-2025 | reviewed 2026-04-29 | pending_clinical_signoff
entries.search_text: reg-zenocutuzumab-nrg1-nsclc zenocutuzumab monotherapy (enrgy) — nrg1-fusion+ nsclc (pan-tumor activity) regimen regimen  src-esmo-nsclc-metastatic-2024 src-nccn-nsclc-2025     enrgy (phase i/ii pan-tumor, n=204): zenocutuzumab is a her2 x her3 bispecific that uniquely blocks nrg1-driven her3 dimerization. nsclc (n=93) orr 37.2%, mdor 14.9 mo, mpfs 6.8 mo. pancreatic adenocarcinoma (n=36) orr 42%. activity independent of fusion partner. fda approval 2024-12 covers both nsclc and pancreatic. nrg1 fusion prevalence ~0.2% pan-cancer; testing gap is the practical bottleneck — dna-only ngs routinely misses nrg1 (large intronic breakpoints), rna fusion assays required. this file is nsclc-anchored (~46% of treated population); same regimen applies to nrg1-fusion+ pancreatic and other solid tumors. generally well-tolerated; infusion reactions + diarrhea + fatigue are dominant aes; rare lvef decreases. zenocutuzumab monotherapie (enrgy) — nrg1-fusion+ nsclc (pan-tumor-aktivität)  sources: src-esmo-nsclc-metastatic-2024, src-nccn-nsclc-2025 | reviewed 2026-04-29 | pending_clinical_signoff therapieschema

entries.subtitle: sources: SRC-ESMO-GASTRIC-2024, SRC-NCCN-GASTRIC-2025 | reviewed 2026-04-30 | pending_clinical_signoff
entries.search_text: reg-zolbetuximab-chemo zolbetuximab + mfolfox6 (spotlight) — 1l cldn18.2-positive her2-negative gastric/gej regimen regimen  src-esmo-gastric-2024 src-nccn-gastric-2025     spotlight (shitara lancet 2023) registrational: zolbetuximab + mfolfox6 vs mfolfox6 in cldn18.2+ (≥75% 2+/3+) her2- 1l metastatic gastric/gej — mpfs 10.6 vs 8.7 mo (hr 0.75); mos 18.2 vs 15.5 mo (hr 0.75). glow (shah nat med 2023) parallel capox backbone — consistent benefit (mos 14.4 vs 12.2 mo). fda approval oct 2024. cycle-1 nausea/vomiting is the principal tolerability challenge — triple-antiemetic prophylaxis + slow infusion mandatory; tolerance improves cycles 2+. hierarchy when multiple actionable signals co-occur: her2+ trastuzumab supersedes; msi-h pembrolizumab supersedes; otherwise cldn18.2+ → zolbetuximab. stub pending clinical co-lead sign-off; bibliographic record src-spotlight-shitara-2023 and src-glow are available; clinical claim linkage requires dual clinical sign-off. zolbetuximab + mfolfox6 (spotlicht) — 1l cldn18,2-positiv her2-negativ gastrisch/gej  sources: src-esmo-gastric-2024, src-nccn-gastric-2025 | reviewed 2026-04-30 | pending_clinical_signoff therapieschema
